stem: Which element is found in proteins but **not** in carbohydrates?

options.rationale: Carbohydrates also contain carbon.
Carbohydrates also contain hydrogen.
Proteins contain nitrogen; carbohydrates do not.
Carbohydrates also contain oxygen.

explanation: Carbohydrates contain carbon, hydrogen and oxygen only. Proteins contain these three elements and nitrogen (and sometimes sulfur).

stem: Glycogen is made from many molecules of which substance?

options.rationale: Glycogen, like starch and cellulose, is a chain of glucose units.
Amino acids join to make proteins.
These make fats and oils.
Sucrose is a disaccharide, not the unit of glycogen.

explanation: Glycogen is a polysaccharide made of many glucose molecules joined together. Animals and fungi store carbohydrate as glycogen.

stem: Fats and oils are made from which smaller molecules?

options.rationale: Glucose units make starch, glycogen and cellulose.
Amino acids make proteins.
One glycerol joined to three fatty acids makes a fat or oil molecule.
These are carbohydrates.

explanation: Fats and oils are built from fatty acids and glycerol (three fatty acids attached to one glycerol).

stem: Match each large molecule with the smaller molecules it is built from.
explanation: Starch and glycogen are both made of glucose; proteins of amino acids; fats of fatty acids and glycerol. Nucleotides make nucleic acids such as DNA, and sucrose is a sugar made of only two units.

stem: True or false: proteins contain only carbon, hydrogen and oxygen.

answerSpec.feedbackTrue: Not true. Proteins also contain nitrogen, and some contain sulfur.
answerSpec.feedbackFalse: Correct. Proteins contain nitrogen as well (and sometimes sulfur).

explanation: Every amino acid contains nitrogen, so all proteins contain carbon, hydrogen, oxygen and nitrogen; some also contain sulfur.

stem: True or false: starch, glycogen and cellulose are all made from glucose.

answerSpec.feedbackTrue: Correct. They differ in how the glucose units are joined and arranged.
answerSpec.feedbackFalse: It is true: all three polysaccharides are built from glucose units.

explanation: Starch (plant store), glycogen (animal and fungal store) and cellulose (plant cell walls) are all polysaccharides made of glucose.

stem: Complete the sentence about the elements in food molecules.

payload.template: Carbohydrates and fats contain carbon, hydrogen and {{blank:a}}; proteins contain these elements and also {{blank:b}}.

explanation: Carbohydrates and fats contain carbon, hydrogen and oxygen. Proteins also contain nitrogen (and sometimes sulfur).

stem: Name the carbohydrate stored in the liver and muscles of animals.

rejected.feedback: Starch is the storage carbohydrate of plants; animals store glycogen.
Glucagon is a hormone; the stored carbohydrate is glycogen.
Glucose is stored by joining it into glycogen.

explanation: Animals (and fungi) store carbohydrate as glycogen, mainly in the liver and muscles. It is made of many glucose units.

stem: Name the small molecules that join together in chains to make proteins.

rejected.feedback: Fatty acids, with glycerol, make fats and oils.
Glucose units make starch, glycogen and cellulose.
Nucleotides make nucleic acids such as DNA.

explanation: Proteins are long chains of amino acids. There are about 20 different amino acids, and their order decides which protein is made.

stem: Which of these carbohydrates is a disaccharide?

options.rationale: Glucose is a monosaccharide (one sugar unit).
Fructose is a monosaccharide.
Sucrose is made of two sugar units: glucose and fructose.
Starch is a polysaccharide made of many glucose units.

explanation: Disaccharides are made of two sugar units joined together: sucrose (glucose + fructose), maltose (glucose + glucose) and lactose (glucose + galactose).
hints: Di- means two: which sugar is made of two sugar units?

stem: Lactose is the sugar found in milk. Which two sugar units is it made of?

options.rationale: Two glucose units make maltose.
Glucose and fructose make sucrose.
This pair does not make any of the common disaccharides.
Lactose is made of glucose joined to galactose.

explanation: Lactose is a disaccharide of glucose and galactose. Maltose is glucose + glucose and sucrose is glucose + fructose.
hints: Lactose contains glucose joined to one other sugar.

stem: Match each type of carbohydrate with an example.
explanation: Fructose is a single sugar unit (monosaccharide), maltose two glucose units (disaccharide) and cellulose many glucose units (polysaccharide). An amino acid is not a carbohydrate.
hints: Mono- means one unit, di- two units and poly- many units.

stem: Which of these is a function of lipids in a mammal?

options.rationale: Oxygen is carried by haemoglobin, a protein.

options.content: Insulating the body to reduce heat loss
options.rationale: A layer of fat under the skin reduces heat loss.

options.content: Speeding up chemical reactions as enzymes
options.rationale: Enzymes are proteins.
Antibodies are proteins.

explanation: Lipids act as an energy store, insulate the body (fat under the skin), protect organs, form part of cell membranes and help waterproofing. Carrying oxygen, catalysing reactions and fighting disease are functions of proteins.
hints: Three of the options are jobs done by proteins.

stem: Which of these foods is the richest source of protein?

options.rationale: Sadza is mostly starch.
Sugar is almost pure sucrose.
Cooking oil is almost pure lipid.
Fish such as kapenta are rich in protein.

explanation: Dried fish such as kapenta are rich in protein. Sadza is mainly starch, sugar is sucrose and cooking oil is lipid.

stem: Nyasha eats a meal of sadza, beans and covo (a leafy green vegetable).

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Beans are rich in protein. Name the element found in protein that is not found in starch.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: The cell walls of the covo contain a polysaccharide that humans cannot digest. Which one?

options.rationale: Humans digest starch with amylase.
Cellulose forms plant cell walls and passes through the human gut as fibre.
Glycogen is found in animals and fungi, not in plant cell walls.
Sucrose is a disaccharide and is digested.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: After the meal, Nyasha's liver stores some of the glucose from the sadza as glycogen. Suggest **two** reasons why glycogen is a better storage molecule than glucose.

points.description: Glycogen is insoluble, so it does not dissolve / leak out of the cells
It does not affect osmosis (water movement) in the cells / it is compact, so a lot can be stored in a small space

parts.explanation: Glycogen is insoluble, so it stays inside the liver cells instead of dissolving and leaking out, and it does not affect the movement of water into and out of the cells by osmosis. Its large, compact molecules also store a lot of glucose in a small space.

explanation: Proteins contain nitrogen (and sometimes sulfur) as well as C, H and O. Cellulose in plant cell walls cannot be digested by humans and acts as fibre. Glycogen is a good store because it is insoluble and compact.
hints: Which element do amino acids contain that sugars do not?

stem: Describe **four** functions of lipids in living organisms. [4]

points.description: Energy store / they release about twice as much energy per gram as carbohydrates
Insulation: fat under the skin reduces heat loss
Protection: fat around organs such as the kidneys cushions them
Waterproofing, e.g. the waxy cuticle of leaves or oil on feathers

answerSpec.modelAnswer: Lipids are a concentrated energy store: they release about twice as much energy per gram as carbohydrates. A layer of fat under the skin insulates the body and reduces heat loss, and fat around organs such as the kidneys protects them from knocks. Lipids are also part of every cell membrane, and waxy lipids waterproof surfaces such as the cuticle of a leaf.

explanation: Lipids store energy, insulate, protect, form membranes and waterproof surfaces.
hints: Think about energy, heat, protection, cells and water.

stem: Describe **four** functions of proteins in the human body, giving an example of each. [4]

points.description: Enzymes that speed up reactions, e.g. amylase
Growth and repair / structure, e.g. keratin in hair, collagen in skin, muscle proteins

answerSpec.modelAnswer: Proteins act as enzymes that speed up chemical reactions, such as amylase, which digests starch. They are used for growth and repair and for structure, for example keratin in hair and nails and collagen in skin. Haemoglobin is a transport protein that carries oxygen in red blood cells. Antibodies, which help to destroy pathogens, are proteins, and so are some hormones, such as insulin.
answerSpec.markingNotes: Any four functions, each with a suitable example.

explanation: Proteins have many roles: enzymes, structural proteins, transport proteins, antibodies and some hormones.
hints: Think of a protein that speeds up reactions, one in blood and one that fights disease.

stem: A student wrote: "Fats are made of glucose molecules joined together." Which correction is right?

options.content: Fats are made of amino acids joined together.
options.rationale: Amino acids make proteins.

options.content: Fats are made of fatty acids and glycerol.
options.rationale: Glucose units make starch, glycogen and cellulose.

options.content: Fats are made of sucrose molecules joined together.
options.rationale: Sucrose is a sugar, not the unit of fats.
Fats are not made of glucose.

explanation: Fats and oils are made from fatty acids and glycerol. Glucose molecules are the units of starch, glycogen and cellulose.
hints: Which two kinds of molecule join together to make a fat?

stem: A substance from an egg contains carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen and sulfur. It is made of long chains of small units of about 20 different kinds. What is it?

options.rationale: Carbohydrates contain no nitrogen or sulfur.
Fats contain no nitrogen and are made of fatty acids and glycerol.
Glycogen is made of one kind of unit (glucose) and contains no nitrogen.
Chains of about 20 kinds of amino acid, containing nitrogen and sometimes sulfur.

explanation: Only proteins contain nitrogen and sulfur among these, and they are made of about 20 different kinds of amino acid joined in chains. Egg white is mostly protein.
hints: Which group is built from about 20 kinds of unit?

stem: Which of these formulae could be a carbohydrate?

options.rationale: Carbon, hydrogen and oxygen, with twice as many hydrogen atoms as oxygen atoms (this is glucose).
It contains nitrogen, so it cannot be a carbohydrate (this is an amino acid).
Far more than twice as many hydrogen as oxygen atoms: this is a fatty acid.
Six hydrogen atoms to one oxygen atom: this is ethanol, an alcohol.

explanation: Carbohydrates contain only carbon, hydrogen and oxygen, usually with hydrogen and oxygen atoms in the ratio 2 : 1, as in glucose, C₆H₁₂O₆.
hints: Check for nitrogen, then compare the numbers of hydrogen and oxygen atoms.

stem: Birds that migrate thousands of kilometres store fat rather than glycogen before they set off. What is the main advantage?

options.content: Fat releases about twice as much energy per gram as glycogen.
options.rationale: So the bird carries less mass for the same energy, which makes long flights possible.

options.content: Fat is easier to digest than glycogen.
options.rationale: Stored fat is used by respiration in the bird's own cells; it is not digested from the gut.

options.content: Fat contains nitrogen, which the bird needs for flight.
options.rationale: Fat contains no nitrogen.

options.content: Fat is soluble, so it can be carried in the blood more easily.
options.rationale: Fat is insoluble in water.

explanation: Lipids release about twice as much energy per gram as carbohydrates. Storing energy as fat means a migrating bird carries far less extra mass than it would if it stored the same energy as glycogen.
hints: Compare the energy released per gram by fats and carbohydrates.

stem: True or false: humans cannot digest cellulose, so it passes through the gut as fibre.

answerSpec.feedbackTrue: Correct. Cellulose provides fibre, which helps food move through the intestines, but no energy.
answerSpec.feedbackFalse: It is true: humans have no enzyme that digests cellulose.

explanation: Cellulose is made of glucose, but humans have no enzyme to break it down. It passes through the gut as dietary fibre, helping food to move along the intestines.
